TRK-02.here: attribution.js carries gclid, gbraid, wbraid, fbclid, msclkid and utm_* onto /booking and /gift; the Hooga session tested /anniversary?gclid=TEST123 → /booking?gclid=TEST123&… (CONVERSION-PLAN §10). Hospitable's widget keeps utm_* but drops gclid, fbclid and _gl, and checkout ends on booking.hospitable.com. Workaround: CONVERSION-PLAN §11 (UTMs on every ad, optimise on booking_handoff, test the source parameter: TRK-08). Re-run on 20 Nov with tools/hooga-attribution-flow.mjs on a production build of b24f110: gclid and the UTMs reached /booking and /gift, and all four dataLayer events (occasion_landing_view, fork_view, select_conversion_path, booking_handoff) carried the gclid. The site's side works; the gap is Hospitable's alone.

UI-02.here: Lab stand-in, not field data: Lighthouse 12.2.1 mobile (simulated slow 4G), median of 3 runs, on a production build of b24f110 served locally with gzip. LCP: /anniversary 9.9 s, /yurt 9.2 s, / 54.9 s, /s/anniversary 155 s (good is 2.5 s or less). CLS 0 and blocking time 0 ms on all four, so the layout and the JavaScript are fine; the weight is the problem. First paint takes 6.3–7.1 s: the fonts are about 1 MB of TTF files (Montserrat-Variable.ttf alone is 673 KB), and none of the @font-face rules in index.css sets font-display. The story deck /s/<occasion> (where the Meta ads will point) downloaded about 117–120 MB: funnelConfig.js uses the original 5.9–9.7 MB PNG and JPEG photos rather than the optimised WebP copies, and its four videos download in full. / uses the 9.7 MB carriage-hot-tub.jpeg (FunnelEntryView.jsx) as well as its 15.5 MB background video. Expected: Pete deferred the speed pass until the product looks right, and it must be done before any paid traffic (CONVERSION-PLAN §0). Re-check with field data once there's traffic.

Nothing on the landing pages or the story deck is under 24 px, chips and tabs included. The only small targets are the footer links on /gift, /stays, /faq and /contact: 16 px tall, in rows 24 px apart. They pass on WCAG's spacing exception, with no margin to spare.

targets.name: What one extra booked night is worth
targets.basis: The margin on a night that would otherwise stay empty (midweek and off-season). Waiting on margin per night (brief §10 Q1).

targets.name: What one direct booking that replaces an Airbnb booking is worth
targets.basis: Only the fee saved by booking direct, net of Hospitable Direct costs. Waiting on the Airbnb share and fee (brief §10 Q2).

targets.name: Most a booking can cost (ads)
targets.basis: What the booking is worth (weighted by how many bookings are extra) minus the profit Pete wants from it. Waiting on brief §10 Q1–Q4.

targets.name: Lowest landing → booking conversion rate at which ads pay
targets.basis: Cost per click ÷ most a booking can cost. Waiting on the above and on real CPCs from the first campaigns. (CONVERSION-PLAN §7 illustrates: at £3 a click, 2% means £150 per booking; that is an illustration, not a target.)

targets.name: Baseline period
targets.basis: For the first 4–8 weeks after launch, record landing → fork, fork → hand-off and hand-off → booking rates rather than setting goals (PLAN.md §9).
